timeline.title: A Short History of Staying Close
items: The first stamp
The Penny Black, the world's first sticky postage stamp, made it easy to post a letter to someone far away.
A voice down a wire
Alexander Graham Bell made the first telephone call, and distance suddenly felt a lot smaller.
The first email
Ray Tomlinson sent the first email between two computers. Love letters would never be the same.
A day for grandparents
The United States named a National Grandparents Day, thanks to the hard work of Marian McQuade.
today: A whole newspaper, posted with love, because some news is too special for a text.

items: The distance is nothing when one has a motive.

The Book of Proverbs
Grandparents sort of sprinkle stardust over the lives of little children.
Alex Haley
Absence makes the heart grow fonder.
An old saying
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: we miss you, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Missing Someone
items: moon
The same Moon
Wherever we are, we all see the same face of the Moon. Look up tonight and we are looking too.
heart
A hug down the phone
One study found a loved one's voice on the phone calmed children almost as much as a hug.
home
Smells like home
Smell is wired close to the brain's memory centres, so one sniff can take you right back.
globe
Orca grandmothers
Killer whale grandmothers lead their pods to food and help their grandchildren survive.
paw
Elephants remember
Elephant herds are led by older females whose memory guides the family to water in hard times.
tree
The grandparent effect
Some scientists think grandparents helping with children is one reason humans live so long.
facts.hand: Still, nothing explains how {who} feels so close from so far.

note.title: What we believe family is
paras: We make newspapers for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe distance is just a number. Love finds its way through phone calls, parcels and paper, and it arrives every time, a little warmer than it left.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not a quick message on a screen, but real pages you can hold, full of news, faces and little voices from home.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you are missed more than you could ever know.
note.wish: Until the next big hug, {who}. We love you.
